note: Clinton County Conservation refuge near Baldwin, in a wooded valley on Bear Creek. Drive-in back-in pads on a one-way road; primitive and youth sites also exist across the road and creek. Sites sit in the wooded valley, mostly back from the creek. --Claude
summary: Fees $30/$30 -> $25 walk-in/$30 reservable; count added 26; year-round with water off Oct 15-Apr 15; 4 reservable at 1 year/5 days. Weak creekside lead at the NE end only.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (weak, upward), stored 'not waterfront' holds for most of the campground. County campground map overlaid on imagery + Esri z19: Bear Creek (about 8-10 m wide, so creek-sized) curves past the NE end. Pads at the NE end (labelled A, B and site 2) are about 20-35 m from the creek through scattered trees with no road between; the middle pads east of the road (10, 12, 14, 16) have about 30-40 m of open mown lawn then brush to the creek; sites 20-26 on the west row are across their own road and about 60-80 m from the creek through a grove. I can't see whether A and B are RV pads (map doesn't say and they aren't among the 26 numbered sites). Unsure after all sources, so it stays not waterfront unless AWH reads the NE end as creekside. County says 'nestled along the tranquil banks of Bear Creek' (marketing).
Stored fees note said '$30 a night reserved' only; the low is the $25 walk-in rate.

Pads: 52 ft x 11 ft back-in gravel (Site 11). Pin at the road bend beside the exit and site 26, about 175 m from mid-campground (42.0482,-90.8537); fine. Phone 563-847-7202 confirmed as the county office; site pages also give the host/park supervisor at 563-357-4134.
